sections.text:
Idris, peace be upon him, is one of the first prophets of God, and it is said that he is one of the ancestors of the Prophet Noah, peace be upon him.

In his time, humanity had gradually begun to deviate from the monotheism that Adam, peace be upon him, had left them with.

Idris saw that some people were beginning to follow their desires and move away from God's commands, so he decided to combat corruption.

God chose him for his message, and gave him great wisdom and abundant knowledge that had not been given to anyone before him.

Idris, peace be upon him, is considered the first person in human history to write with a pen and write newspapers and sermons with it.

He taught his people how to write and blog, which contributed to preserving science and transmitting it between generations.

He was also the first to sew and wear clothes, as people before him used to wear the skins of animals they hunted.

Idris made a needle from bones, and began sewing cloth and making clothes to cover the body and protect it from the heat of summer and the cold of winter.

Idris was not limited to worldly knowledge, but rather he was abundant in knowledge of matters of religion and the afterlife.

He used to think a lot about the creation of the heavens and the earth, and about the greatness of the Creator, Glory be to Him.

Idris called his people with a wise manner and good preaching, and a group of righteous people came to believe with him.

But the majority were arrogant and rejected his call, so Idris decided to emigrate with those who believed with him to search for a new land in which to establish the religion of God.

They arrived in the land of Egypt, where they settled and began spreading the call for monotheism, justice, and equality.

Idris divided his time regularly: days to teach and guide people, and days to isolate himself to worship God and meditate.

God taught him astronomy and the movement of stars and planets, as well as arithmetic and mathematics.

He established rules and laws for his nation that would help them organize their lives and build a cohesive and strong society.

He always warned them against the deceit of Satan, and reminded them of the story of their father Adam, peace be upon him.

Idris was known by the nickname “The Triangle of Grace,” because he was blessed with prophecy, wisdom, and kingship.

Despite his high status, he was very humble, eating from the work of his own hands and thanking God for every blessing.

Because of his intense sincerity and his frequent worship and fasting, God loved him with great love.

God praised him in the Holy Qur’an, describing him as one of the righteous and patient prophets.

God was not satisfied with praising him, but rather honored him with a dignity that no one else had attained in his time, which was being raised to heaven.

God Almighty said: “And mention in the Book Idris. Indeed, he was a truthful prophet * and We raised him to a high place.”

The interpreters differed about the meaning of being raised. Some of them said that he was raised alive to the fourth heaven as the Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, saw him during the journey of the Night Journey and Mi’raj.

Among them are those who said that elevation means raising one’s status and high status in this world and the hereafter thanks to one’s knowledge and piety.

Idris, peace be upon him, left a great legacy of knowledge and morals, and was a role model for all who came after him in diligence and good work.

The moral of his story is that knowledge and work must go together. Worldly knowledge, such as writing and sewing, is no less important than religious knowledge.

The righteous person is the one who populates the earth with construction and industry, and populates his heart with monotheism and worship.
